ferment_lexeme_watch.transliteration: ḥnq (uncertain semantic class in relevant early passages)
ferment_lexeme_watch.TLA_commentary: The lexeme occurring in Pyramid Texts 64c, 90a-b and 91a-b and Coffin Texts VI 356o has been translated by van der Molen as 'ferment (?)' and by Hannig as Gärstoff/Ferment, while other interpretations treat it as a liquid/juice; TLA explicitly preserves the uncertainty.
ferment_lexeme_watch.rule: Do not use this lexeme as proof of kombucha, SCOBY, bacterial cellulose, vinegar culture or a specific fermentation technology.

corpus_parallel_search.negative_result: No ancient Egyptian text was identified in this pass that combines raw papyrus manufacture, washing, cross-layering, pressing, drying, writing, and fermentation into one attested production recipe.
corpus_parallel_search.interpretation: The strongest overlap is procedural vocabulary and a directly attested sequence involving writing on a freshly washed papyrus sheet. Pressing/flattening, joining, drying and writing are individually attested lexemes, but combining them into the JANUS BIOPAPYRUS workflow is a modern reconstruction.
